newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia central bank sees 97 gold output at 100 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Russia central bank sees 97 gold output at 100 tonnes.

text.p: Russian gold output in 1997 will be no more than 100 tonnes, Itar-Tass news agency on Tuesday quoted a senior central bank official as saying.
Sergei Kyshtymov, head of the bank's precious metals department and one of its most senior precious metals officials, said the forecast was 11-12 percent below 1996 gold output.
Other officials have variously forecast gold production at 95-110 tonnes this year. Official estimates for 1996 range from 100.8-124 tonnes.
Kyshtymov was also quoted as confirming the central bank's gold reserves were about 400 tonnes. He said the bank was ready to buy all domestic gold mined this year.
The bank said in March that it aimed to boost its gold stocks by nearly 90 tonnes a year over 1997 and 1998.

Tass quoted unnamed experts at the Association of Russian Banks -- which is battling bureaucratic muddles to win the right to finance gold output -- as saying gold output could fall this year to a miserly 80 tonnes.
